maria: AtlasResell just flagged a settlement problem for March: our invoice was USD but GCP paid out in EUR and their settlement shows a double FX conversion. They claim a shortfall of ~€120. Can someone triage? :confused:
ashok: Can you paste the invoice line and the settlement row they sent?
maria: Invoice (our PDF):
```
INV-2026-03-6022
SKU: redwood_search_c1
Qty: 350
Unit price (USD): $0.95
Line net (USD): $332.50
```
Partner settlement CSV row (as received from GCP):
```
sku,units,unit_settled,currency,unit_settled_ccy,platform_fee_ccy
redwood_search_c1,350,0.95,EUR,0.88,12.32
```
maria: The partner says GCP converted $0.95 -> €0.88 using their March FX table, but then AtlasResell's own accounting system converted back to USD using a different rate, effectively double-applying FX and leaving them short. They expected settlement equivalent to $332.50 less fees; instead they received €308.00 which converts back to $300.20 with their rate -> shortfall ~$32.30, but their downstream ledger also shows VAT rounding issues so they report a gross shortfall of €120.
billing-bot: export job for merchant=atlasresell on 2026-03-31 complete. Export id: GCP-EXP-1800152468. Pricing profile used: PROFILE_COMMITTED_15. Settlement currency tag: EUR (partner configured EUR settlements). FX metadata attached: gcp_fx_table_2026_03 (EUR/USD 0.9263).
ashok: So GCP paid out in EUR by design (partner settlement currency), but partner's accounting system re-converted to USD separately. The double conversion shouldn't affect the payout we owe to the reseller, but we need to honor the contract currency semantics. Does our reseller agreement guarantee USD-denominated commissions or EUR-settlements?
luca: Finance check: AtlasResell contract (s3://contracts/atlasresell/reseller-agmt-2025.pdf) specifies commission and payouts in USD unless partner opts into EUR settlement. Their onboarding form shows they selected EUR settlement for VAT handling on 2026-03-01. If they selected EUR, we bill the buyer in USD but remit the reseller in EUR per GCP settlement.
sophie: Partner claims they did NOT opt into EUR at signup; they attached a signed onboarding scan showing USD. GCP partner-bot: ticket GP-100233 opened. GCP responds that their partner console shows AtlasResell settlement currency = EUR as of 2026-03-02 (possible manual change).
billing-bot: merchant_profile for atlasresell: settlement_currency=EUR, commission_pct=10, merchant_flags=[settle_eur=true]. Merchant create_ts=2024-11-12. Last merchant update: 2026-03-02 by user id 8934 (ui: partner-console).
ashok: Looks like settlement currency flipped in GCP/partner console on Mar 2, which might not match AtlasResell internal intent. Regardless, GCP paid in EUR and we recorded the export in EUR. Partner's complaint is that their accounting reconverted EUR->USD using a stale rate causing the larger €120 figure; they want Redwood to reimburse conversion delta as a goodwill gesture.
maria: Finance: what's the exposure? If we reimburse conversion deltas for EUR-settled partners we'd open the floodgates. But this is a messy customer experience if the partner truly didn't intend EUR. We need docs: 1) proof partner selected EUR (or didn't), 2) our export showing EUR settlement, 3) GCP ticket and audit trail for change, 4) computed delta.
james: (not in thread list) -- omitted
kelly: AP policy: we do not reimburse FX conversion losses unless Redwood caused the currency flag switch or mis-exported currency metadata. We can consider a one-time goodwill credit up to €150 if engineering or partner-console logs show a Redwood-originated change. Need legal sign-off for amounts > €100.
sophie: I've attached partner onboarding scan and their email claiming they didn't enable EUR: s3://partners/atlasresell/onboarding-scan-2024.pdf. GCP ticket GP-100233 shows partner-console change by user id 8934 (internal GCP admin). I've asked GCP for the admin email and timestamp.
nashok: billing-bot, who initiated the merchant_profile update that set settlement_currency to EUR in our system? Any calls from our side to change settlement currency?
billing-bot: No internal change recorded. merchant_profile.last_updated_by: external_sync_service@gcp-integration (job id: sync-2026-03-02-07). Source of truth: GCP partner sync. No Redwood-initiated change.
luca: Legal: if GCP changed partner-view and partner claims they didn't authorize, we can request GCP to reverse or issue correction. But for goodwill we can offer a provisional credit of up to €100 while GCP investigates. Kelly, can AP approve a provisional €100 credit memo pending GCP confirmation?
kelly: I can approve a provisional credit memo CM-2026-03-031 for €100 as a customer experience gesture, provided it's labeled provisional and recoverable if GCP reverses. Need reconciliation export link and GCP ticket. Also need a short statement clarifying this is a one-time goodwill and not a policy precedent.
maria: Files attached: export https://internal.redwood/billing/exports/1800152468 (md5:7c4a8d09ca3762af61e59520943dc264), s3://redwood-billing/gcp/recon/2026-03/atlasresell-fx-1800152468.csv, GCP ticket GP-100233. Computed delta per partner workbook: €120 (includes conversion delta + VAT rounding). Our internal calc: settlement (EUR) = €308.00 -> using partner's stale rate back to USD = $300.20. Using GCP FX table back to USD => $332.50 -> implied delta ~$32.30; partner's ledger rounding/VAT complaint inflates to €120.
ashok: Recommended path: 1) issue provisional goodwill CM-2026-03-031 for €100 pending GCP audit 2) Sophie to escalate GP-100233 and request audit trail and admin id 8934 identity 3) Engineering/partner-ops to add alert when settlement_currency changes between buyer invoice and partner settlement for the same merchant.
elly: (typo) kelly: I'll prepare the provisional CM and route for e-sign with the provisional wording and recovery clause. Posting ETA 2 business days.
sophie: I'll tell the partner we've issued provisional €100 credit and we're pushing GCP for audit; ask them to hold off on further escalation for 5 business days.
